questions.question:
Statement: All the employees of the firm were given a bonus this year.

Conclusions:
I. Ravi, an employee of the firm, received a bonus this year.
II. Some employees of the firm did not receive a bonus this year.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: The statement says every employee got a bonus, so Ravi did too (I follows) and no employee missed out (II contradicts it). Answer: Only conclusion I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: The shop remains closed on Sundays.

Conclusions:
I. The shop is open on Mondays.
II. The shop does no business on Sundays.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: A shop that is closed on Sundays does no business on Sundays (II follows). The statement says nothing about Mondays, so I does not follow. Answer: Only conclusion II follows.

questions.question:
Statement: In a class of 40 students, 36 passed the test.

Conclusions:
I. Some students did not pass the test.
II. Every student passed the test.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: 40 − 36 = 4 students did not pass, so I follows and II is false. Answer: Only conclusion I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: No one under 18 is allowed to vote in the election.

Conclusions:
I. A 17-year-old cannot vote in the election.
II. Everyone aged 18 or above will vote in the election.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: A 17-year-old is under 18, so cannot vote (I follows). The statement says who is allowed to vote, not who will vote, so II does not follow. Answer: Only conclusion I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: The company will hire only graduates for this post.

Conclusions:
I. A person who is not a graduate will not be hired for this post.
II. Every graduate will be hired for this post.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: "Only graduates" makes graduation necessary, so I follows. It does not promise that every graduate is hired, so II does not follow. Answer: Only conclusion I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: The rain has stopped, but the roads remain flooded.

Conclusions:
I. The roads are still flooded although it is not raining now.
II. It is still raining.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: The statement directly gives I and denies II. Answer: Only conclusion I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: Some cars in the showroom are electric, and all electric cars have zero tailpipe emissions.

Conclusions:
I. Some cars in the showroom have zero tailpipe emissions.
II. All cars in the showroom are electric.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: The electric cars in the showroom have zero tailpipe emissions, so I follows. Only "some" cars are electric, so II does not follow. Answer: Only conclusion I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: Only members of the club may use its swimming pool.

Conclusions:
I. A person who is not a member cannot use the pool.
II. Every member uses the pool.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: "Only members" makes membership necessary, so I follows. Nothing says members actually use it, so II does not follow. Answer: Only conclusion I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: The price of petrol was increased by 10% last month.

Conclusions:
I. The price of petrol before last month was lower than it is now.
II. The price of diesel also rose last month.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: A 10% increase makes the new price higher than the old, so I follows. Diesel is not mentioned, so II does not follow. Answer: Only conclusion I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: A survey found that 70% of the residents of a city own a two-wheeler.

Conclusions:
I. 30% of the residents do not own a two-wheeler.
II. Every resident owns a two-wheeler.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: 100% − 70% = 30% do not own one, so I follows and II is false. Answer: Only conclusion I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: Either the meeting will be held on Monday or it will be postponed to the next week.

Conclusions:
I. If the meeting is not held on Monday, it will be postponed to the next week.
II. The meeting will certainly be held on Monday.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: The either-or statement gives I directly. It does not say which alternative happens, so II does not follow. Answer: Only conclusion I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: Students who submit the project on time get extra credit.

Conclusions:
I. Rohit submitted the project late, so he did not get extra credit.
II. Meena submitted the project on time, so she got extra credit.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: II applies the rule directly. The rule says nothing about students who submit late (they might get credit another way), so I does not follow. Answer: Only conclusion II follows.

questions.question:
Statement: The factory's output rose in March, but its profits fell.

Conclusions:
I. The factory produced more in March than before.
II. The factory's costs must have risen in March.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Output rising is stated, so I follows. Profits can fall for reasons other than costs (for example lower prices), so II does not follow. Answer: Only conclusion I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: No train from Platform 1 goes north, and some trains from Platform 2 go north.

Conclusions:
I. No northbound train leaves from Platform 1.
II. All trains from Platform 2 go north.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: I restates the first part of the statement. Only some Platform 2 trains go north, so II does not follow. Answer: Only conclusion I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: The government has announced a subsidy for farmers who own less than 2 hectares of land.

Conclusions:
I. A farmer with 1.5 hectares of land is eligible for the subsidy.
II. A farmer with 3 hectares of land will not receive the subsidy.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: 1.5 is less than 2, so I follows. The statement does not say that others are excluded, so II does not follow. Answer: Only conclusion I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: Of the 120 candidates who appeared, 90 passed the written test, 60 passed the interview, and 40 passed both.

Conclusions:
I. Exactly 10 candidates passed neither.
II. Exactly 50 candidates passed only the written test.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Passed at least one = 90 + 60 − 40 = 110, so 120 − 110 = 10 passed neither (I). Only the written test: 90 − 40 = 50 (II). Both follow. Answer: Both conclusions follow.

questions.question:
Statement: If the signal is red, the car stops. The car did not stop.

Conclusions:
I. The signal was not red.
II. The signal was red.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: The contrapositive of "if red then stops" is "if not stopped then not red", so I follows and II contradicts it. Answer: Only conclusion I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: Every applicant who clears the test is called for an interview. Some applicants who were called for an interview were rejected.

Conclusions:
I. Some applicants who cleared the test were rejected.
II. Some applicants who were called for an interview did not clear the test.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: The statement does not say that only those who cleared the test are called, so the rejected interviewees may not have cleared it. Neither conclusion is forced. Answer: Neither conclusion follows.

questions.question:
Statement: Either the printer is faulty or the cable is loose. The cable has been checked and is tight.

Conclusions:
I. The printer is faulty.
II. The printer is not faulty.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: The cable is not loose, so the printer must be faulty. I follows and II contradicts it. Answer: Only conclusion I follows.

questions.question:
Statement: To pass the examination, a student must score at least 40% in each subject.

Conclusions:
I. A student who scores 35% in one subject does not pass.
II. Every student who passed scored at least 40% in each subject.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Scoring at least 40% in each subject is required for passing, so a student with 35% in one subject fails (I) and every passer met the requirement (II). Both follow. Answer: Both conclusions follow.
